title: Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored
body:
## Overview

Multi-column (2 to 80 activation columns) mul_mat_vec_q for reordered K-quant and Q8_0 weights on the Intel XMX matrix engines (int8 DPAS, ESIMD), for the SYCL backend. It targets speculative decoding verification (2 to 8 tokens per step) and short prompt batches (9 to 80 tokens). Three types also use it for a single column (Q2_K, Q3_K, Q8_0).


## Additional information

The existing multi-column dp4a kernels redo the weight unpack and the per-column scale arithmetic for every column, so the cost grows with the batch size (about 5 lane operations per dp4a per extra column). Profiling showed the step time for 4 tokens was 46% above 1 token on a Q6_K model, and much worse for Q3_K. Decode of one token is bandwidth bound, speculative
verification is not, so this gap is important.

Hardware and setup: Intel Arc Pro B70 (32 GB), Windows 10, oneAPI 2026.1 (icx), Level Zero driver
1.15.37858, SYCL backend with `GGML_SYCL_F16=ON`, graphs on. `llama-bench -ngl 99 -fa 1 -r 3`.
All models are Qwen3.8 27B variants (qwen35 architecture). "Before" is the same build with
`GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_XMX=0`. Values are tokens per second, `ppN` is a batch of N tokens, so the step
time is N / value.

| Model (GB) | tg1 | pp2 | pp4 | pp8 | pp16 | pp32 |
| Q8_0 (29.0) | 15.9 -> 18.0 | 30.6 -> 36.0 | 58.4 -> 70.7 | 108.8 -> 133 | 32.4 -> 241 | 64.3 -> 266 |
| Q6_K (22.4) | 22.8 -> 22.8 | 41 -> 44.6 | 63 -> 86 | 79 -> 159 | 45 -> 210 | n/a |
| Q4_K_S (16.4) | 26.5 -> 26.5 | 41.1 -> 48.4 | 67.7 -> 90 | 82.7 -> 131 | 50.3 -> 308 | 99 -> 354 |
| Q3_K_S (12.7) | 28.9 -> 33.1 | 27.2 -> 62 | 44.7 -> 115 | 66.6 -> 192 | 36.2 -> 243 | 71.7 -> 269 |
| Q2_K (10.8) | 33.4 -> 37.6 | 31.3 -> 69 | 50.8 -> 121 | 71.9 -> 169 | 46.6 -> 235 | 91.9 -> 266 |

End to end with speculative decoding (--spec-type draft-mtp, n-max 4, p-min 0.5, temperature 0.75, 5 prompts of 400 tokens, average tokens per second; the trim column also sets LLAMA_MTP_DRAFT_VOCAB=98304):

| Model | XMX off | XMX on | XMX on + trim |
| Q8_0 | 32.4 | 40.3 | 43.1 |
| Q4_K_S | 38.7 | 47.6 | 51.0 |
| Q3_K_S | 28.6 | 53.6 | 57.2 (63 in a later run) |
| Q2_K | 30.2 | 60.0 | 63.9 |
| Q6_K (earlier run, no p-min) | about 35 | n/a | about 55 |

Run to run noise is about 1 to 3 tokens per second on the end to end numbers (sampling).

Done:
- Each kernel was compared with the existing dp4a kernel for the same layer, on real model tensors, at 1, 2, 4, 7 and 8 columns: normalized MSE about 1e-14 for all six types (differences are float summation order only). This was done with a temporary check inside the dispatch, which is not in the tree.
- test-backend-ops test -o MUL_MAT -b SYCL0: 1132/1132 passed. NOTE: those cases use small `k` (below 1024), where the new kernel declines, so this shows no regression elsewhere but does not exercise the kernel.
- `llama-perplexity` (24 chunks of 512 tokens, text from `docs/`, `-b 32 -ub 32` so the prompt uses the kernel), Q3_K_S: 4.8360 XMX off), 4.8349 (XMX on), 4.8360 (batch 512). Q6_K, Q4_K_S and Q2_K also match within 0.003 (table at the end). Q8_0 not measured.
- Greedy generation with speculative decoding is identical for the first 1200 to 1900 characters with the kernel on or off and then diverges slightly (summation order).

Not done:
- Only one GPU model (Arc Pro B70) and one driver. Other Intel GPUs (Xe, Xe2, Arc A-series, Data Center) are untested. `load_2d`, DPAS shapes and the register file sizes are architecture dependent. The 2D block load and DPAS paths are guarded by `__has_include` only, not by a device check.
- Only qwen35 models. MoE (`MUL_MAT_ID`) is untouched. Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, IQ types are untouched.
- `test-backend-ops` has no case that reaches the kernel (needs `k >= 1024`).
- The full local CI (ci/README.md) was not run.
- KL divergence versus a high precision reference was not measured.
